description: Writes the interviewed draft out as a bundle directory, checks its shape and soundness, and hands it back as the job's result.

interview.description: the bucket the interview node produces, accumulated key by key over every turn: `graph` from the last turn that reported one, `skills` from the last turn that settled a manifest

graph.description: the graph document the interview settled, whole

skills.description: one manifest per node of that graph, WITHOUT `hash`. NOT `required`, and deliberately: since t464 a turn reports `skills` only when it settled a manifest, so nothing in the interview's own output schema GUARANTEES the key — an interview abandoned before any manifest existed really does arrive here without it, and `unproduced_input` (`domain/graph.ts`) is right to refuse a pin this bundle could not keep. What the map owes is a manifest per node; a delivery that finds fewer says so in `checked.problems` rather than being stopped at the gate

bundle.description: the same draft, written out and checked: this is what the next step registers or exports

checked.description: what the validator answered, so a person reads a verdict and not a claim

note.description: one line: what the map covers, and anything the interview left rough

preconditions: the interview settled a map: `input.interview.graph`, and one manifest per node at `input.interview.skills`
the session may write inside its own working directory

checks.description: The draft is held against the same validator that guards the bundles committed in this repository — structure and the four soundness rules. One violation is EXPECTED and is not a defect: `node_with_contract` also asks each node for a pinned `hash`, and a draft has none, because computing the pin belongs to whoever registers (D4). Report it as such; every other violation is a real one.

instructions:
# Deliver the interviewed map as a bundle

The interview is over. What you have is the map it settled — the graph document
at `input.interview.graph` and one skill manifest per node at
`input.interview.skills` — and what this step owes is a bundle somebody can look
at and decide about.

## Write it out

In the directory you are in, write:

```
draft/graph.json          `input.interview.graph`, exactly as the interview left it
draft/skills/<id>.json    one file per entry of `input.interview.skills`, named after its own `id`
```

Write them as they came. **Do not improve the map here.** If something is wrong
with it, that is a finding you report, not a thing you fix: the person answered
those questions, and a step that silently edits their answers makes the whole
interview unreviewable.

## Check it

Run the check this node declares:

```
node scripts/validate-graph.mjs draft/graph.json
```

It answers two things — is the document structurally a graph, and is its topology
a sound workflow net: one entry, every node reachable, every node able to reach a
final one, no dangling edge. Report **what it answered**, in `checked`, whether
it passed or not.

One violation is expected and is not a defect: the `node_with_contract` rule also
asks each node for a pinned `hash`, and a draft has none. Name it in `problems`
and say so in the note; treat every OTHER violation as real.

Then check by hand the two things the validator cannot:

- there is exactly one manifest per node, and each node's `skill_ref` names an
  `id` and a `version` that a manifest in `draft/skills/` really has;
- **no manifest carries a `hash`**. The pin is computed by whoever registers the
  bundle; a hash written here is a pin that will not close, and D4's whole point
  is that a pin which does not close stops the map.

## Report

```resultado
{"bundle": {"graph": {…}, "skills": [{…}]},
 "checked": {"structure": true, "soundness": true, "problems": []},
 "note": "<one line: what this map covers, and anything the interview left rough>"}
```

A draft that did not pass is still reported — with `structure` or `soundness`
false and every problem named in `problems`. Registering is not yours and never
was: a person reads this and decides.
